exposure: size at birth (e.g., smaller than average)
cohort: The study included a total weighted sample of 133,448 live births from demographic and health surveys conducted between 2014 and 2024 in 31 Sub-Saharan African countries.
finding: The neonatal mortality rate in sub-Saharan Africa was 32 per 1000 live births, with maternal occupation, home delivery, caesarean section, twin births, higher birth order, and smaller size at birth being significantly associated with increased odds of neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Caesarean section and home delivery were significantly associated with higher odds of neonatal mortality, with caesarean section having an AOR of 1.58 and home delivery an AOR of 1.29.
followup_time: 28 days (implied by the definition of neonatal mortality)
cross-section timing: Data from demographic and health surveys conducted between 2014 and 2024
birth_weight: Size at birth (categorized as smaller than average vs. average/larger)
